entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sisenna Statilius Taurus, a scion of the distinguished Statilii Tauri family, served as a Roman senator and achieved the coveted consulship in 16 CE alongside Lucius Scribonius Libo. His career unfolded during the crucial transition from the reign of Augustus to that of Tiberius, a period demanding a delicate balance between traditional republican ideals and the consolidating power of the Principate. Descended from a prominent Augustan-era general and consul, Titus Statilius Taurus, Sisenna represented the senatorial elite who navigated this evolving political landscape, maintaining a semblance of aristocratic influence while serving the burgeoning imperial administration.

During his consulship, Sisenna Statilius Taurus would have presided over senatorial meetings, enacted legislation, and performed various civic and religious duties customary for Rome's highest magistracy. His tenure coincided with Tiberius's early years as emperor, a time marked by the suppression of conspiracies and the consolidation of imperial authority, often masked by deference to the Senate. While specific details of Sisenna's individual actions during this year are not extensively documented in literary sources, his participation underscores the continued functioning of the traditional Roman political system, even as its true power shifted decisively towards the emperor. Inscriptions, rather than comprehensive histories, remain our primary window into his public life, attesting to his official roles and familial connections.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sisenna Statilius Taurus represents the continuity of senatorial influence and administrative stability during the critical early years of the Roman Principate under Tiberius, helping legitimize the new imperial order. His career exemplifies the evolving role of the Roman aristocracy in adapting to the realities of imperial rule.
